edit.description: pendingGate: read targetFence.writablePaths/entryChannelPaths inside run(), not at construction

list pendingGate under 'Use the built-ins first'; show lazy-construction pattern (get gates() accessor) for declaration-driven fences; the existing hand-rolled pending-parse example predates the builtin (v0.8 §6) and should point at it

summary: pendingGate captures targetFence eagerly at construction; declaration-driven chains need it read at run() time

per.section: 6. `pendingGate`: composed validation and fence pre-check as a builtin

tests.asserts: a targetFence whose writablePaths/entryChannelPaths are populated after pendingGate(...) is called (e.g. a getter-backed Phase) is still correctly fence-checked when run() executes

acceptance: pendingGate reads targetFence fields inside run(), not eagerly; a fence populated after construction is respected; CHAIN-AUTHORING.md documents pendingGate with the lazy-construction pattern
notes: Dogfood chain.ts is unaffected (module-level buildFence constant) — this is the second-implementation case: a chain deriving its fence from per-job declaration.json, per engine-boundary.md.

per.section: 2. Entry schema splits: engine core + chain-declared extension

edit.description: §4 handshake bullet overclaims a hard-stop guarantee that requires the invoking binary to already be >=0.7

summary: MIGRATING-0.8.md §4 promises the pin handshake is a hard stop without noting it can't fire from a pre-0.7 global binary
acceptance: §4's handshake bullet states the hard-stop only fires once the invoking global binary itself contains the handshake (>=0.7); names that a 0.6.x global predates the check and silently runs the upgraded chain instead
notes: Scope-correction only, low-risk. Does not resolve the structural blind spot — see open question on the handshake's threat model for a pre-handshake engine.
